prompt: What is the first thing a hosted observability product replaces for a small team?
hint: The lab is about twenty containers.

choices.text: The need to instrument the services
The work of running, upgrading and backing up the stack
The three signals, with a fourth that covers all of them
The trace id, which hosted products do not need

prompt: Match each feature a hosted product sells to what it is.

pairs.right: timings measured in the customer's browser
which functions spend the CPU in production
what the user saw before an error

prompt: Which of this course's lessons stop applying once a team buys a hosted product?

choices.text: The ones about cardinality, since the vendor absorbs it
The ones about sampling, since storage is unlimited
choices.why: It bills for every span kept.

choices.text: None: the products are judged on the same ideas
The ones about logs, since vendors index everything for free

prompt: Why does the section give each product's billing unit and not its price?

choices.text: Because the products are free below a certain size
Prices change and vary by contract; the unit decides which habit costs
Because every product uses the same price per unit
Because prices are secret and never published

prompt: Which product instruments the processes on a host without anybody changing code?

choices.text: Sentry, through the SDK inside each app
choices.why: An SDK is code inside the app.

choices.text: Dynatrace, with OneAgent
New Relic, through its OTLP endpoint
choices.why: An endpoint receives; it does not instrument.

choices.text: Zipkin, through its dependency graph
choices.why: Zipkin is a store, not a product here.

prompt: Which of the four products can you run on your own servers?

choices.text: Datadog
New Relic
Dynatrace
choices.why: Not the one the section names.

choices.text: Sentry

prompt: Where was the lock-in of the older, agent-based products?
hint: What had to change to leave?

choices.text: In the price of the first year
choices.why: Leaving was hard for another reason.

choices.text: In the instrumentation written against the vendor's library
In the network between the services
choices.why: The network was not the vendor's.

choices.text: In the databases, whose schema each vendor's agent rewrote for its own use
choices.why: The data was the services' own.

prompt: What rule keeps the choice of vendor open?

choices.text: Instrument with OpenTelemetry and keep vendor code at the edge
Use two vendors at once for every signal, always
choices.why: That doubles the bill and keeps nothing open.

choices.text: Never send data to a vendor at all
Write instrumentation with each vendor's library in turn

prompt: A vendor accepts OTLP. What should an evaluation still check?

choices.text: Whether OTLP is faster than the vendor's own protocol
Whether the vendor charges for OTLP data separately
choices.why: Not the concern the section raises.

choices.text: Which features need the vendor's own agent
Whether the Collector supports the vendor's region
choices.why: The Collector sends to any URL.

prompt: What does an error tracker record?

choices.text: Every request, with its timing
Exceptions, each with its stack and context
Every log line at `INFO` and above
The CPU time of each function

prompt: What are breadcrumbs in an error tracker's event?

choices.text: The frames of the stack, from the top down
The other errors in the same issue
Log records kept in memory, sent only if an error follows
Links to the traces of the same request, added by the Collector before the event is sent

prompt: How does the server turn ten thousand events into one line on a screen?

choices.text: By the message text, compared word by word with the events already in the issue
By grouping events with the same stack into an issue
By keeping only the first event and discarding the rest
By the release, one line per version
choices.why: Releases are a field of the issue.

prompt: One bug raises the same exception from two different call sites. How does grouping by stack show it?

choices.text: As one issue, since the exception type is the same
As two issues
As none, since duplicates are dropped
As one issue per user who met it

prompt: Why did the card number reach the event?

choices.text: The script logged it with `log.info`
choices.why: The logs did not mention the card.

choices.text: The coupon code contained it
It was a local variable, and the SDK sends them by default
The Collector copied it into the event from the checkout's trace on the way out

prompt: After the fix, the value of `card` in the event reads `[___]`.
Why is an error tracker in a region abroad a matter for the LGPD?

choices.text: Because error trackers are forbidden in Brazil
Events hold what was in scope, personal data included, and storing them abroad is a transfer
Because the LGPD requires all logs to be in Portuguese
Because a vendor abroad deletes the data after a week, which breaks the retention that the law requires of you

prompt: To send every trace to a hosted product as well as to Jaeger, what has to change in the services?
hint: The Collector is in the middle.

choices.text: Nothing: the Collector gets one more exporter
Each service gets a second exporter, pointed at the vendor's intake
Each service gets the vendor's key
The services switch from OTLP to the vendor's own protocol

prompt: Why does the lab's Collector read the vendor's key from the environment?

choices.text: Because the exporter cannot read keys from files
choices.why: It could; that is the problem.

choices.text: Because the key changes on every request
choices.why: It is the same on every request.

choices.text: To keep the secret out of the repository with the configuration
Because environment variables are encrypted by Docker before the process reads them

prompt: The vendor stops answering. What happens to the traces going to Jaeger?
hint: Each exporter has its own queue.

choices.text: They stop too, until the vendor recovers
They slow down to match the vendor's retries
Nothing: only the vendor's queue fills
They are sent twice, once for each destination
choices.why: Each exporter sends its own copy once.

prompt: The vendor's queue filled 28 of 1000 places in 75 seconds. At that rate, how many minutes until it is full? Answer to the nearest five.
A team adds a `user_id` label to a metric sent to a hosted product. Which unit of the bill grows?

choices.text: Hosts
choices.why: The number of machines did not change.

choices.text: Custom metric series
Users with a full seat
Gigabytes of logs ingested each month

prompt: A team leaves a vendor after two years, with OpenTelemetry in every service. What still has to be rebuilt?
hint: What is written in the vendor's language.

choices.text: The instrumentation of every service
Dashboards, alert rules and saved searches
choices.why: Right; and the history stays behind.

choices.text: The Collector, which only works with one vendor
Nothing at all

prompt: A five-person team has no one who wants to run Prometheus, Loki and Jaeger, and its customers are in Brazil. What is the most defensible plan?
hint: Who runs it, where the data goes, and what stays portable.

choices.text: Run the open-source stack anyway, since it is free
A hosted product with a suitable region, fed through a Collector, services on OpenTelemetry
A hosted product with its agent inside the business code, for the extra features
No observability until the team grows

prompt: Put the steps of evaluating a hosted product in a sensible order.
hint: Measure before asking for a price.
items: Measure your volume in the product's own unit
Add the product as one more exporter in the Collector
Check which features need its own agent
Ask for a quote at twice the measured volume

prompt: Match each finding of this lesson to the earlier lesson whose idea it repeats.

pairs.left: a card number in an error event
a bill per custom metric series
